note: Aegis-curated validation playbooks. Every playbook needs reviewedBy, lastReviewed and https sources. {host} is replaced with the analyst's target in the page.

playbooks.summary: HTTP/2 flow-control window overflow in NGINX (heap overflow in a worker process; possible remote code execution). Exposure requires an affected NGINX build AND HTTP/2 enabled on a listener reachable by the attacker. Data-plane only.
conditions: An affected NGINX Open Source, NGINX Plus or NGINX-based F5 product version is running (see fixed versions).
HTTP/2 is enabled on at least one server block ('http2 on;' or 'listen … http2'), or via an ingress controller setting.
The HTTP/2 listener is reachable by an attacker (internet-facing raises priority, but internal exposure still counts).

fixedVersions.fixed: No fixed release listed by Rapid7 — follow F5 K000163926
5.8.0 (first version outside the NVD range — confirm in F5 K000163926)
2.9.0 (first version outside the NVD range — confirm in F5 K000163926)
5.16.2 (first version outside the NVD range — confirm in F5 K000163926)
Fixed package release in the Red Hat / Ubuntu advisory (backported; the upstream version string may not change)

steps.title: Find every running NGINX master process on the host
steps.positive: One line per NGINX instance. Check the version and config of each (containers included).
steps.negative: No NGINX master process on this host. Check containers and Kubernetes separately.

steps.title: Is HTTP/2 enabled in the effective configuration?
steps.positive: Matching lines mean HTTP/2 is enabled. With an affected version, record as Validated (version + configuration).
steps.negative: No output means HTTP/2 isn't enabled in this instance's configuration. Run it for every instance; nginx -T includes all included files.

steps.title: Ingress controller HTTP/2 settings
steps.positive: 'http2: "true"' (F5 NGINX Ingress Controller) or 'use-http2: "true"' (community ingress-nginx) means HTTP/2 is on.
steps.negative: No key found: the controller default applies. Community ingress-nginx enables HTTP/2 by default; F5 NGINX Ingress Controller does not. Confirm in your controller's documentation.

steps.title: Does the listener negotiate HTTP/2? (curl)
steps.positive: '2' means HTTP/2 is negotiated and reachable from where you ran it.
steps.negative: '1.1' means HTTP/2 isn't offered on this listener. Repeat for every HTTPS port and virtual host.

steps.title: Does the listener advertise h2 via TLS ALPN? (Nmap)
steps.positive: 'h2' in the tls-alpn output means HTTP/2 is offered.
steps.negative: Only http/1.1 is listed: HTTP/2 isn't offered on that port.

steps.title: Does the listener accept h2? (OpenSSL, no extra tools)
steps.positive: 'ALPN protocol: h2' means HTTP/2 is accepted.
steps.negative: 'No ALPN negotiated' means HTTP/2 isn't offered over TLS on this port.

steps.title: Look for worker crashes that may indicate exploitation attempts
steps.cmd: sudo grep -hE 'worker process [0-9]+ exited on signal (6|11)' /var/log/nginx/error.log* 2>/dev/null | tail -20
steps.positive: Repeated worker crashes (signal 11 = segmentation fault) on an affected, HTTP/2-enabled build are a possible attack indicator. Escalate to incident response and preserve logs.
steps.negative: No crashes logged. This does not prove no attempt occurred (logs may rotate or go elsewhere).

steps.title: After upgrading or changing configuration, validate and reload
steps.cmd: sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
steps.positive: 'syntax is ok' / 'test is successful', then a clean reload. Upgrade to a fixed version per the table. If F5 K000163926 lists it as a mitigation, disabling HTTP/2 ('http2 off;' / removing 'http2' from listen) reduces exposure until you can patch.
steps.negative: A config test error means the reload was not applied. Fix the reported line first.

steps.title: Confirm the fixed version is the one actually running
steps.positive: A fixed version, and a master process started after the upgrade, means remediated. Re-run the HTTP/2 checks to record the final state.
steps.negative: An old version, or a master process older than the upgrade, means the new binary isn't running yet (restart required).

mitigations: Upgrade to the fixed release for each affected product (see table).
Until patched, reduce exposure: restrict access to HTTP/2 listeners where possible, and follow any interim mitigation in F5 K000163926.
Enable or keep ASLR on (default on modern Linux); the description notes code execution is easier where ASLR is disabled or bypassed.
notes: No public Nuclei template or official Nmap script is indexed for this CVE. Rapid7 states InsightVM/Nexpose have an unauthenticated check (19 Nov 2026 content).
Aegis does not provide or reference exploit code. Version + configuration + exposure is enough to validate this CVE.
